17	# LaTeX 论文写作全流程
18	
19	ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. 工作模式
24	
25	开始前选择模式：
26	
27	| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
28	|------|------|------|
29	| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
30	| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
31	| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论
36	
37	**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**
38	
39	### 2.1 一句话贡献
40	
41	在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。
42	
43	### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map
44	
45	为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：
46	
47	| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
48	|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
49	| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
50	| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
51	| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |
52	
53	**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**
54	
55	### 2.3 章节起草顺序
56	
57	```
58	1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
59	2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
60	3. Related Work
61	4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
62	```
63	
64	### 2.4 Quality Gates
65	
66	投稿前必须通过：
67	- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
68	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
69	- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
70	- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
71	- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）
76	
77	**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**
78	
79	### 3.1 黄金法则
80	
81	```
82	IF 无法程序化获取引用:
83	    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
84	    → 明确告知用户
85	    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
86	```
87	
88	### 3.2 五步验证流程
89	
90	```
91	1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
92	2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
93	3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
94	4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
95	5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
96	```
97	
98	### 3.3 API 速查
99	
100	| API | 用途 | 限制 |
101	|-----|------|------|
102	| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
103	| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
104	| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |
105	
106	```python
107	# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
108	import requests
109	def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
110	    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
111	                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
112	    r.raise_for_status()
113	    return r.text
114	
115	# Semantic Scholar 搜索
116	from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
117	sch = SemanticScholar()
118	results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
119	for p in results:
120	    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
121	```
122	
123	### 3.4 引用处理规则
124	
125	| 情况 | 处理 |
126	|------|------|
127	| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
128	| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
129	| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
130	| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
131	| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 4. 顶会模板速查
136	
137	### 4.1 ML/AI 会议
138	
139	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
140	|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
141	| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
142	| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
143	| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
144	| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
145	| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
146	| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |
147	
148	### 4.2 系统会议
149	
150	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
151	|------|---------|---------|---------|
152	| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
153	| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
154	| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
155	| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |
156	
157	### 4.3 模板使用原则
158	
159	```bash
160	# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
161	cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/
162	
163	# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
164	latexmk -pdf main.tex
165	
166	# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
167	```
168	
169	**禁止事项：**
170	- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
171	- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
172	- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 5. 写作规范
177	
178	### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）
179	
180	花**大致相等**的时间在：
181	1. Abstract
182	2. Introduction
183	3. 图表
184	4. **其余所有内容加起来**
185	
186	审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。
187	
188	### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）
189	
190	```
191	1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
192	2. 为什么这很难且重要
193	3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
194	4. 有什么证据
195	5. 最惊人的数字/结果
196	```
197	
198	删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~
199	
200	### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）
201	
202	| 原则 | 规则 |
203	|------|------|
204	| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
205	| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
206	| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
207	| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |
208	
209	### 5.4 常见修改
210	
211	| 问题 | 修复 |
212	|------|------|
213	| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
214	| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
215	| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
216	| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |
217	
218	---
219	
220	## 6. 投稿工程链
221	
222	### 6.1 构建
223	
224	```bash
225	# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
226	latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex
227	
228	# 手动：需要多次编译
229	pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
230	```
231	
232	### 6.2 Lint + 格式化
233	
234	```bash
235	# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
236	chktex main.tex
237	
238	# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
239	latexindent -w main.tex
240	```
241	
242	### 6.3 图表格式
243	
244	| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
245	|------|------|------|
246	| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
247	| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
248	| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |
249	
250	```latex
251	\usepackage{booktabs}
252	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
253	\toprule
254	Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
255	\midrule
256	Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
257	\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
258	\bottomrule
259	\end{tabular}
260	```
261	
262	**图表规范：**
263	- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
264	- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
265	- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
266	- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）
267	
268	### 6.4 投稿打包
269	
270	```bash
271	# 清理辅助文件
272	latexmk -c
273	
274	# 打包投稿
275	zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
276	```
277	
278	### 6.5 常见失败点
279	
280	| 问题 | 解决 |
281	|------|------|
282	| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
283	| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
284	| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
285	| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
286	| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |
287	
288	---
289	
290	## 7. 会议转投
291	
292	当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：
293	
294	### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换
295	
296	| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
297	|------|---------|---------|
298	| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
299	| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
300	| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
301	| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |
302	
303	### 7.2 转投原则
304	
305	1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
306	2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
307	3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
308	4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 8. 投前清单
313	
314	### 通用清单
315	
316	- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
317	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
318	- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
319	- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
320	- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
321	- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
322	- [ ] 符合页数限制
323	- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
324	- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
325	- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning
326	
327	### 会议特定
328	
329	| 会议 | 额外要求 |
330	|------|---------|
331	| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
332	| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
333	| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
334	| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
335	| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |
336	
337	---
338	
339	## 参考资源
340	
341	**写作方法论：**
342	- [Neel Nanda: How to Write ML Papers](https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/eJGptPbbFPZGLpjsp/) — What/Why/So What 框架
343	- [Farquhar: How to Write ML Papers](https://sebastianfarquhar.com/on-research/2024/11/04/how_to_write_ml_papers/) — 五句法 Abstract
344	- [Gopen & Swan: Science of Scientific Writing](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~swanson/papers/science-of-writing.pdf) — 读者预期 7 原则
345	- [Lipton: Heuristics for Scientific Writing](https://www.approximatelycorrect.com/2018/01/29/heuristics-technical-scientific-writing-machine-learning-perspective/) — 用词
346	- [Perez: Easy Paper Writing Tips](https://ethanperez.net/easy-paper-writing-tips/) — 微观清晰度
347	
348	**API：**
349	- [Semantic Scholar](https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/) | [CrossRef](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/) | [arXiv](https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/)
350	
351	**会议官方：**
352	- [NeurIPS](https://neurips.cc/) | [ICML](https://icml.cc/) | [ICLR](https://iclr.cc/) | [ACL](https://www.aclweb.org/) | [AAAI](https://aaai.org/) | [EMNLP](https://2025.emnlp.org/)

# LaTeX 论文写作全流程

ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。

---

## 1. 工作模式

开始前选择模式：

| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
|------|------|------|
| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |

---

## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论

**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**

### 2.1 一句话贡献

在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。

### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map

为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：

| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |

**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**

### 2.3 章节起草顺序

```
1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
3. Related Work
4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
```

### 2.4 Quality Gates

投稿前必须通过：
- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta

---

## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）

**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**

### 3.1 黄金法则

```
IF 无法程序化获取引用:
    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
    → 明确告知用户
    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
```

### 3.2 五步验证流程

```
1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
```

### 3.3 API 速查

| API | 用途 | 限制 |
|-----|------|------|
| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |

```python
# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
import requests
def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.text

# Semantic Scholar 搜索
from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
sch = SemanticScholar()
results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
for p in results:
    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
```

### 3.4 引用处理规则

| 情况 | 处理 |
|------|------|
| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |

---

## 4. 顶会模板速查

### 4.1 ML/AI 会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |

### 4.2 系统会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |

### 4.3 模板使用原则

```bash
# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/

# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
latexmk -pdf main.tex

# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
```

**禁止事项：**
- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`

---

## 5. 写作规范

### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）

花**大致相等**的时间在：
1. Abstract
2. Introduction
3. 图表
4. **其余所有内容加起来**

审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。

### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）

```
1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
2. 为什么这很难且重要
3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
4. 有什么证据
5. 最惊人的数字/结果
```

删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~

### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）

| 原则 | 规则 |
|------|------|
| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |

### 5.4 常见修改

| 问题 | 修复 |
|------|------|
| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |

---

## 6. 投稿工程链

### 6.1 构建

```bash

latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex

# 手动：需要多次编译
pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
```

### 6.2 Lint + 格式化

```bash

chktex main.tex

# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声

```

### 6.3 图表格式

|------|------|------|
| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |

\midrule

```

**图表规范：**
- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）

# 打包投稿

```

|------|------|

Web corpora increasingly contain machine-generated text.
Recent estimates place the synthetic fraction at 20--60\% of crawled data~\citep{cheng2025contamination}, and this share grows as language models are deployed for content production at scale.
Training on such contaminated data has concrete consequences: \citet{shumailov2024model} show that recursive training on model outputs leads to irreversible quality degradation---\emph{model collapse}---and \citet{dohmatob2025strong} prove under scaling-law regimes that even a vanishingly small synthetic fraction suffices to trigger this failure mode, ruling out data scaling as a remedy.
A central difficulty is that the contamination proportion in any given corpus is unknown: synthetic text enters through diverse, uncoordinated channels with no centralized provenance record.
The prevalence, severity, and opacity of synthetic contamination make contamination-aware pretraining a practical necessity.

A natural response is \emph{detect-and-reweight}: train a classifier to estimate each sample's synthetic probability $q(x)$, then suppress likely-synthetic samples via the weighting function $w(x) = (1 - q(x))^b$.
\citet{drayson2025detection} demonstrate this approach for model collapse prevention and show that the exponent $b$ critically determines outcomes---their optimal values range from $b{=}10$ for models at ${\leq}360$M parameters to $b{=}1$ at 1.7B, and misspecification degrades results substantially.
Selecting $b$ therefore requires per-model validation-set grid search, with computational cost scaling linearly in the number of candidates (six training runs in a typical sweep).
Other approaches assume even stronger supervision: \citet{he2025golden} derive theoretically optimal weights from convergence analysis but require the exact contamination ratio $\rho$, which is precisely what is unavailable in practice.
Hard detection-and-removal strategies~\citep{feng2025beyond} discard borderline samples entirely, sacrificing the smooth reweighting that continuous $q$-scores enable.

Given per-sample detector scores $q(x)$, how should one choose $b$ without a validation set or known contamination proportion?
We formulate this as a dual-constrained optimization over each training batch: find the smallest $b$ that ensures the weighted effective real proportion $\aeff(b)$ reaches a quality threshold $\tau$, while keeping Kish's effective sample size $\mathrm{ESS}(b)$ above a stability floor $\nmin$.
The quality constraint has theoretical grounding: convergence rate under contaminated training improves with the effective real-data fraction~\citep{wang2026survive}, motivating a lower bound on $\aeff$.
The stability constraint prevents extreme weight concentration that degrades gradient quality.
These two requirements exhibit a natural opposition.
$\aeff(b)$ increases monotonically in $b$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:monotone}), yielding a lower bound $\btau$---the minimum exponent needed to achieve the target quality.
$\mathrm{ESS}(b)$ decreases monotonically, yielding an upper bound $\bess$---the maximum exponent before gradient stability degrades.
The adaptive exponent $\bstar = \btau$ when the feasible region $[\btau, \bess]$ is non-empty, embodying a \emph{minimum intervention principle}: apply the least downweighting sufficient to meet the quality target, preserving as much effective training data as possible.
When the constraints conflict ($\btau > \bess$), the stability ceiling takes precedence.

This minimum-intervention semantics distinguishes the method from the alternative of maximizing $b$ subject only to ESS stability.
Among batches that require reweighting, the dual-constraint solver selects $\bstar$ via the $\aeff$ bound in 40\% of cases, with mean $\bstar{=}1.67$; the ESS-only variant would choose $b{=}4.15$ in these same batches, 2.5$\times$ more aggressive.
The remaining 49.9\% of batches have sufficient real-data content to skip reweighting entirely ($\bstar{=}0$).
The per-batch $\bstar$ distribution (median 0.87, mean 1.40) adapts continuously to each batch's contamination composition without any held-out signal.

On Qwen3-0.6B continued pretraining with 40\% synthetic contamination (132M+ tokens from FineWeb), adaptive reweighting achieves mean held-out perplexity of 17.651 across three seeds, matching the grid-searched optimum ($b{=}0.5$, mean 17.646) within seed-to-seed variance (\S\ref{sec:results}).
The grid sweep requires six complete training runs to identify this optimum; the adaptive method requires one.
The ESS-only variant (maximum intervention) yields mean PPL 17.722---worse than the uniform baseline (17.694)---confirming that maximum intervention degrades training while minimum intervention improves it.
A lightweight TF-IDF + Logistic Regression detector (AUC\,=\,0.939, calibrated ECE\,=\,0.048) suffices throughout, suggesting that score calibration matters more than raw classification accuracy for provenance-based reweighting.

Our contributions:
\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
\item A dual-constrained framework for adaptive exponent selection: $\bstar = \inf\{b \geq 0 : \aeff(b) \geq \tau\}$ subject to $\mathrm{ESS}(b) \geq \nmin$, computed per-batch from detector scores with minimum-intervention semantics (\S\ref{sec:method}).
\item Empirical evidence that adaptive $\bstar$ matches grid-searched best within seed variance at zero validation cost, and that minimum intervention (dual constraint) outperforms maximum intervention (ESS-only) across three seeds (\S\ref{sec:results}).
\item A demonstration that a lightweight TF-IDF + LR detector with calibrated $q$-scores supports effective reweighting, achieving results comparable to stronger neural detectors (\S\ref{sec:experiments}).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Main Comparison}

Table~\ref{tab:main} reports held-out perplexity across methods and seeds.
Adaptive reweighting achieves comparable performance to grid-best: PPL 17.653 vs.\ grid-best $b{=}0.3$ at 17.640 (seed 42), a gap of 0.013 that falls within the range of cross-seed standard deviation (${\sim}0.007$).
This comes at zero validation cost---grid search requires $|\mathcal{B}|$ complete training runs (seven in our sweep), whereas adaptive requires one.

The grid-$b$ sweep reveals monotonically increasing PPL from $b{=}0.3$ to $b{=}5.0$ (17.640 to 17.818 on seed 42), confirming that exponent selection is consequential.
The optimal $b{=}0.3$ differs from the $b{=}10$ reported by \citet{drayson2025detection} at comparable model scale, underscoring the model-dependence of fixed-exponent selection.

ESS-only (maximum intervention) yields mean PPL $17.723 {\pm} 0.006$ across three seeds, providing no improvement over uniform ($17.694 {\pm} 0.008$).
Removing $\aeff$ and maximizing $b$ subject only to $\mathrm{ESS} \geq \nmin$ over-downweights borderline samples, providing direct evidence for the minimum-intervention principle.

The Golden Ratio oracle~\citep{he2025golden} achieves PPL 17.654 (seed 42) using known provenance labels.
Adaptive reaches 17.653 on the same seed without provenance access, suggesting the dual constraint recovers near-optimal weights from noisy detector scores alone.

The adaptive $\bstar$ distribution (median 0.87, IQR $[0.54, 1.51]$, mean 1.40) confirms that most batches need only moderate intervention.
Among the 50.1\% of batches requiring reweighting, $\aeff$ is the binding constraint in 40.1\% of cases (mean $\bstar{=}1.67$); the ESS-only variant would select $b{=}4.15$ in these same batches---$2.5{\times}$ more aggressive.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccc@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & \textbf{Seed 42} & \textbf{Seed 123} & \textbf{Seed 456} & \textbf{Mean} \\
\midrule
Uniform               & 17.694 & 17.686 & 17.702 & 17.694 \\
Grid-best ($b{=}0.3$)$^\dagger$ & \textbf{17.640} & --     & --     & --     \\
Grid ($b{=}0.5$)       & 17.651 & \textbf{17.638} & \textbf{17.650} & \textbf{17.646} \\
ESS-only               & 17.730 & 17.720 & 17.719 & 17.723 \\
Golden Ratio$^\ddagger$ & 17.654 & --     & --     & --     \\
\midrule
Adaptive (ours)        & 17.653 & 17.643 & 17.657 & 17.651 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Held-out perplexity (PPL, $\downarrow$) at $\rho{=}0.4$.
Grid-best selects the optimal fixed $b$ post-hoc from seven candidates.
$^\dagger$Seed 42 only; cross-seed pending.
$^\ddagger$Requires known provenance labels (oracle); seed 42 only.
Best per column in \textbf{bold}.}
\label{tab:main}
\end{table}

\subsection{Sensitivity Analysis}

\paragraph{Quality threshold $\tau$.}
Table~\ref{tab:tau} varies $\tau$ while holding $n_{\min} = 2$ (seed 42).
All values in $\tau \in [0.5, 0.8]$ improve over uniform, with $\tau = 0.8$ achieving the lowest PPL (17.653).
Higher $\tau$ demands greater $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$, forcing the solver to increase $b^*$: mean $\bar{b}^*$ rises monotonically from 0.39 at $\tau{=}0.5$ to 3.08 at $\tau{=}0.95$.
Below 0.8, reweighting is too gentle to fully exploit the detector signal; above, $b^*$ inflates past diminishing returns and PPL degrades.
The range $[0.5, 0.8]$ provides a wide safe operating region, with $\tau = 0.8$ as the recommended default.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}cccc@{}}
\toprule
$\tau$ & \textbf{PPL} & $\Delta_{\mathrm{unif}}$ & $\bar{b}^*$ \\
\midrule
0.50 & 17.688 & $-$0.006 & 0.39 \\
0.60 & 17.681 & $-$0.013 & 0.59 \\
0.70 & 17.679 & $-$0.015 & 0.89 \\
\textbf{0.80} & \textbf{17.653} & $\mathbf{-0.041}$ & \textbf{1.40} \\
0.90 & 17.712 & $+$0.018 & 2.36 \\
0.95 & 17.723 & $+$0.029 & 3.08 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Sensitivity to $\tau$ (seed 42, $n_{\min}{=}2$, $\rho{=}0.4$).
$\Delta_{\mathrm{unif}}$: PPL change vs.\ uniform baseline (17.694).
$\bar{b}^*$: mean adaptive exponent across batches.}
\label{tab:tau}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Minimum ESS $n_{\min}$.}
Removing the ESS floor ($n_{\min} = 1$) allows $b^*$ to inflate to mean 7.20, degrading PPL to 17.789---0.095 worse than uniform.
At $n_{\min} = 2$ ($= \lfloor B/2 \rfloor$ for batch size $B{=}4$), PPL stabilizes at 17.653; $n_{\min} = 3$ yields a comparable 17.644.
The coupling $n_{\min} = \lfloor B/2 \rfloor$ provides a configuration-aware default that balances reweighting headroom against gradient stability.

\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main-results}

Table~\ref{tab:main} reports held-out perplexity at $\rho = 0.4$ across three seeds.
Continued pretraining reduces PPL from 22.970 (pretrained checkpoint) to the 17.6--17.8 range; the initial 5.3-point drop absorbs the bulk of easy gains, and all method comparisons operate within this residual.

Adaptive $\bstar$ (mean $17.651 \pm 0.007$) matches grid-best ($b{=}0.5$, mean $17.646 \pm 0.007$) within seed variance, capturing 89.6\% of the improvement from uniform to grid-best: $(17.694 - 17.651)/(17.694 - 17.646)$.
The grid sweep requires six complete training runs to identify $b{=}0.5$ as optimal~\citep{drayson2025detection}; the adaptive method requires one.

ESS-only (mean 17.723) performs worse than uniform (17.694) on all three seeds.
Without the $\aeff$ constraint, the solver maximizes $b$ up to the ESS floor on every batch, concentrating weights on a few high-confidence samples and degrading gradient quality.
The dual constraint is load-bearing: stability alone is insufficient, and maximum intervention degrades rather than improves training.

Golden Ratio~\citep{he2025golden} achieves 17.654 (seed\,42), comparable to adaptive $\bstar$ at 17.653 on the same seed, despite requiring oracle access to the true contamination ratio $\rho$.

\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccc@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & \textbf{Seed 42} & \textbf{Seed 123} & \textbf{Seed 456} & \textbf{Mean} \\
\midrule
Pretrained ckpt        & 22.970 & --     & --     & --     \\
\midrule
Uniform                & 17.694 & 17.686 & 17.702 & 17.694 $\pm$ .008 \\
Grid-best ($b{=}0.5$) & 17.651 & 17.638 & 17.650 & \textbf{17.646} $\pm$ .007 \\
Adaptive $\bstar$ (ours) & 17.653 & 17.643 & 17.657 & 17.651 $\pm$ .007 \\
ESS-only               & 17.730 & 17.720 & 17.719 & 17.723 $\pm$ .006 \\
Golden Ratio$^\dagger$ & 17.654 & --     & --     & --     \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Held-out perplexity ($\downarrow$) on human-authored FineWeb at $\rho{=}0.4$.
Three seeds for Uniform, Grid-best, Adaptive, and ESS-only; Pretrained and Golden Ratio evaluated on seed\,42 only.
Grid-best selected post-hoc from six training runs.
Best 3-seed mean in \textbf{bold}.
$^\dagger$\,Oracle method requiring known $\rho$~\citep{he2025golden}.}
\label{tab:main}
\end{table}


\subsection{Contamination Level Robustness}
\label{sec:robustness}

To test sensitivity to contamination severity, we evaluate at $\rho = 0.6$ (seed\,42 only).
ESS-only (PPL 17.770) falls within 0.004 of uniform (17.766)---maximum intervention provides no benefit at higher contamination.
With more synthetic samples per batch, the ESS floor binds earlier, preventing the solver from raising $b$ enough to suppress them effectively.
Adaptive $\bstar$ (17.740) still improves over uniform by 0.026, though the gap to grid-best ($b{=}0.5$, PPL 17.704) widens from 0.005 at $\rho{=}0.4$ to 0.036.

The asymmetry follows from constraint geometry.
ESS-only pushes $b$ upward until $\mathrm{ESS}$ hits $\nmin$; at higher $\rho$, this ceiling activates sooner.
The dual constraint targets the \emph{minimum} $b$ satisfying $\aeff \geq \tau$, starting from below; even when the stability ceiling caps the exponent before the quality target is met, the quality-first search direction makes more effective use of the feasible range than the maximum-intervention alternative.

These are single-seed results and should be interpreted accordingly; the qualitative pattern---ESS-only collapsing while adaptive $\bstar$ retains benefit---is consistent with the constraint mechanism described above.


\subsection{Hyperparameter Sensitivity}
\label{sec:sensitivity}

The adaptive method has two hyperparameters: quality threshold $\tau$ and ESS floor $\nmin$.
We evaluate sensitivity at $\rho = 0.4$ (seed\,42).

\paragraph{Quality threshold $\tau$.}
Table~\ref{tab:tau} sweeps $\tau$ from 0.50 to 0.95 with $\nmin{=}2$ fixed.
All values in $[0.5, 0.8]$ improve over uniform, with the largest improvement at $\tau{=}0.8$ ($-$0.041 PPL).
The safe range spans 0.035 PPL, and mean $\bstar$ increases monotonically with $\tau$: higher thresholds demand more aggressive reweighting.
Beyond $\tau{=}0.8$, $\bstar$ inflates (mean 2.36 at $\tau{=}0.9$, 3.08 at $\tau{=}0.95$) and PPL degrades past the uniform baseline, as over-aggressive downweighting reduces effective sample size without commensurate quality gains.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}cccc@{}}
\toprule
$\tau$ & PPL $\downarrow$ & $\Delta$ vs.\ Uniform & Mean $\bstar$ \\
\midrule
0.50 & 17.688 & $-$0.006 & 0.39 \\
0.60 & 17.681 & $-$0.013 & 0.59 \\
0.70 & 17.679 & $-$0.015 & 0.89 \\
\textbf{0.80} & \textbf{17.653} & $\boldsymbol{-}$\textbf{0.041} & \textbf{1.40} \\
0.90 & 17.712 & $+$0.018 & 2.36 \\
0.95 & 17.723 & $+$0.029 & 3.08 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Quality threshold sweep (seed\,42, $\nmin{=}2$, $\rho{=}0.4$).
$\Delta$ relative to uniform baseline (PPL\,=\,17.694).
Values in $\tau \in [0.5, 0.8]$ all improve over uniform; $\tau{=}0.8$ is the recommended default.}
\label{tab:tau}
\end{table}

\paragraph{ESS floor $\nmin$.}
At $\nmin{=}1$ (effectively no stability constraint), mean $\bstar$ rises to 7.20 and PPL degrades to 17.789---0.095 above uniform.
The default $\nmin{=}2$ yields the best result (PPL 17.653, mean $\bstar{=}1.40$).
At $\nmin{=}4$ (equal to the micro-batch size $B$), the constraint $\mathrm{ESS}(b) \geq B$ forces $\bstar{=}0$ on every batch, recovering uniform training (PPL 17.695).
The requirement $\nmin < B$ is necessary for the method to operate (\S\ref{sec:method}); $\nmin = \lfloor B/2 \rfloor$ provides a stable default.

Both $\tau$ and $\nmin$ have principled defaults that transfer without per-model tuning, unlike the global exponent $b$ which requires validation-set search.
No knowledge of the true contamination proportion $\rho$ is needed.


\subsection{Constraint Regime Analysis}
\label{sec:regime}

Over 26{,}458 training batches (seed\,42), the dual-constraint solver falls into three regimes:
49.9\% of batches are already sufficiently real-dominated ($\aeff(0) \geq \tau$), yielding $\bstar{=}0$ with no reweighting applied;
20.2\% are $\aeff$-binding, where the quality constraint $\btau$ determines $\bstar$;
and 30.0\% are ESS-binding, where the stability ceiling $\bess$ caps $\bstar$ before the quality target is met.

When $\aeff$ binds, $\bstar$ reflects the minimum intervention needed: the solver stops increasing $b$ once $\aeff(b) \geq \tau$.
An ESS-only solver would push $b$ further in these same batches, suppressing more samples than necessary and discarding gradient signal.
The per-batch $\bstar$ distribution (mean 1.40, median 0.87, std 1.93, range $[0, 20]$) adapts continuously to each batch's contamination composition without any held-out signal.

Method-level PPL differences (${\sim}$0.04 between adaptive and uniform) are small in absolute terms.
These differences arise, however, in a highly optimized regime: continued pretraining has already absorbed a 5.3-point drop from the pretrained checkpoint, and remaining gains are incremental.
Within this range, matching 89.6\% of the grid-searched optimum---without validation runs or knowledge of $\rho$---demonstrates that per-batch dual-constrained adaptation can substitute for global hyperparameter search.
